quizzes.stem: A bank's loan flow must always check identity, then credit, then ask a person to approve, and an interrupted application must not repeat the credit check. Which style fits?

options.a: A single prompt, because the order is stated in the text of the call
options.b: A model-driven loop, because the model picks each next step on its own
options.c: A typed agent, because the loan is a record of fixed shape and size
options.d: A graph, because each node saves state and resumes after a stop

explanation.d: The page says "Checkpointers persist a thread's graph state as checkpoints", and a resumed run "repeats no earlier node", so the credit check is not paid for twice.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the table gives the next step to "The model, at each turn", and the loan order must always be fixed.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a typed agent has "Validated output" but "Types guard the edges of the model's freedom. They do not choose the route."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a prompt keeps no state, and the page gives the graph, not the prompt, the job of resuming: "the run resumes from the last checkpoint".

quizzes.stem: A support agent starts receiving a kind of request that its authors never listed. Which style copes without anyone adding a path for it?

options.a: A loop in which the model chooses each next step
options.b: A graph whose edges pick the next node from the state
options.c: A typed agent whose replies must fit an output schema
options.d: A checkpointer that restores the run to its last state

explanation.a: The page says "The route is whatever the model chooses, so the same code handles a case nobody planned for."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a case you did not draw has no path", and the edges are drawn in advance.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Types guard the edges of the model's freedom. They do not choose the route."
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A checkpoint is a copy of the state at a point in the graph.", which helps a run resume and adds no path.

quizzes.stem: A model-driven loop keeps calling the same tool and never produces a final reply. Which control does the engineering post name for this?

options.a: A checkpoint saved after each tool call
options.b: A longer context window for the whole conversation
options.c: A ceiling on the number of rounds that it is allowed
options.d: A second model that repeats each call to confirm it

explanation.c: The post lists "stopping conditions (such as a maximum number of iterations) to maintain control."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A checkpoint is a copy of the state at a point in the graph.", which saves the state and does not end a loop.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a loop that never ends must be cut off", and a larger window does not give the loop an end.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a repeated call adds cost without a stop, and "Agentic systems often trade latency and cost for better task performance".

quizzes.stem: A team's feature is one model call that summarises a document, with retrieved passages added to the prompt. What does the engineering advice suggest?

options.a: A graph framework with durable state and resume support
options.b: The Messages API alone, refined with in-context examples
options.c: The Agent SDK running Claude Code's loop in the service
options.d: Managed Agents with the session stored on Anthropic's side

explanation.b: The post says "For many applications, however, optimizing single LLM calls with retrieval and in-context examples is usually enough."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A framework earns its place when the feature it brings is one you need and would build badly, and not before.", and one call needs no durable state.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Start from the top and stop at the first row that meets the requirement.", and one call is met by the first row, before the Agent SDK.
explanation.d: Ruled out because Managed Agents is chosen when "The task is long-running or asynchronous", and this is one short call.

quizzes.stem: A framework agent gives odd answers, and nobody on the team can read the exact text it sent to the model. Which cost of frameworks is this?

options.a: Coupling, as state formats follow the framework's releases
options.b: A missing feature, as frameworks offer no tracing hooks
options.c: Unneeded features, as persistence adds code to maintain
options.d: Hidden prompts, as layers obscure the prompts and responses

explanation.d: The post says frameworks "often create extra layers of abstraction that can obscure the underlying prompts and responses, making them harder to debug."
explanation.a: Ruled out because coupling is that "Your state format, your tool definitions and your tests then follow the framework's releases.", which says nothing of reading the prompt.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a framework gives you "tool schemas and parsing, retries, tracing hooks", so the feature is not missing.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Otherwise it is code to maintain." is the cost of features nobody needs, and the symptom here is a prompt nobody can read.

quizzes.stem: A product must survive a restart and resume a long task, and the team does not want to operate the sandbox in which the code runs. Which option is the smallest that fits?

options.a: The Messages API, with a loop that the team writes and stores
options.b: Managed Agents, with the session kept on Anthropic's side
options.c: A graph framework, hosted and upgraded by the team itself
options.d: The Claude Code CLI, started by a person every morning

explanation.b: The table gives Managed Agents the task that is "long-running or asynchronous" for those who want "no sandbox to run", with the session stored by Anthropic.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a loop of your own leaves "The loop, the tools, the state" and the sandbox to the team, which is more than the smallest option.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a graph is chosen when you "need its state, resume or typed output, and will pay in coupling", and the team would still host it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the table row for Managed Agents reads "The task is long-running or asynchronous and you want no sandbox to run", and a person starting a CLI each morning is not a service that resumes.

quizzes.stem: Regulators will audit an approval chain whose steps never change. Which style does the first page match to that need?

options.a: Graph-based, with nodes and edges drawn beforehand
options.b: Model-driven, with the model choosing at each turn
options.c: Typed, with each reply validated against a schema
options.d: A mix in which the model picks the route and a graph logs it

explanation.a: The first page says to use the graph style "when the process is known and must be auditable: an approval chain, an order flow".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the table gives the next step to "The model, at each turn", and "The route is whatever the model chooses".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Types guard the edges of the model's freedom. They do not choose the route."
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The model fills in a node. It does not pick the route."

quizzes.stem: A team wants to be able to replace its agent framework later. Which design choice keeps that cheap?

options.a: Copying the framework's source into the product's repository
options.b: Storing the sessions in the format that the framework defines
options.c: Wrapping each model call and tool in a function of its own
options.d: Importing the framework's types directly in each module

explanation.c: The page says "Keeping the model call behind a thin function of your own limits the damage".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the trap is "Coupling the whole codebase to one framework", and a copy of the source ties the repository to one.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Your state format, your tool definitions and your tests then follow the framework's releases."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the aim is "so that a change of framework is a change in one place", and imports in each module spread the change.
